RSAT has been a reliable option for Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations teams looking to automate regression testing without writing code.
But Dynamics 365 testing rarely stops at F&O.

What happens when your business processes span Sales, Customer Service, Field Service, Business Central, or connected systems? What about integration testing? And how much time does your team spend re-recording tests when release waves change the UI?

These are some of the key limitations that can leave gaps in your regression strategy.

With Microsoft support for RSAT ending on May 15, 2027, now is the time to look beyond what your current regression suite covers—and start defining what your migration strategy needs to address.

Read our latest blog to understand what Dynamics 365 regression testing with RSAT doesn’t cover and what that could mean for your quality strategy.

May 15, 2027 isn’t just another date on the Dynamics 365 roadmap.
 
That’s when Microsoft support for RSAT ends.
 
RSAT may continue to run, but without bug fixes, security patches, feature updates, or guaranteed compatibility with future Dynamics 365 F&O releases, the testing risk shifts to your team.
 
And for organizations with large RSAT libraries, migration isn’t something to leave until the last minute.
 
Now is the time to assess your current coverage, understand the gaps, and start planning what comes next.
 
👉 Read the full RSAT deprecation timeline and what D365 F&O teams should do before 2027:
